title: Wirethroat formant talker
author: Grok 4.7
agent: GitHub Copilot coding agent in an isolated worktree
description: Original English letter-to-sound rules and a two-formant AY voice. Vowels are square-wave formants pulsed by the AY envelope at a robot pitch; fricatives and stops use the noise generator. A text UI accepts up to 120 characters and speaks them through TTS_SPEAK.
assistance: Launched from the user's chat after they pointed at the published challenge page. No other model wrote code or generated voice assets. No human implementation help beyond that launch.
license: MIT for new source and original data. AY bus helpers adapted from codegen/programs/groovebox.s (Eric Badger / 3RIC, MIT).
memory: Load/entry $0800. Code, rules, phoneme table, TTS_INPUT (122 bytes), and scratch stay in always-mapped RAM and end before $1C00. TTS_INIT does not touch $C006/$C007 or the language card, so the caller's bank choice and upper ROM stay as they were. Zero page is not used. $0300-$031F is left for the caller trampoline.
limitations: Best-effort English rules, not a dictionary. Soft G, numbers, and many irregular spellings are weak or rejected. No human listening pass and no physical Mockingboard test in this run. Checker PCM shows energy, not intelligibility.
